I am a Tenured Professor in the Department of Anesthesia and Perioperative Medicine and the Division of Critical Care Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, where I serve as Director of Clinical Research. I am a clinician-scientist with a research focus on sepsis, perioperative complications, and acute kidney injury, with particular emphasis on vasopressor strategies, cardiovascular physiology, and hemodynamic therapies.  A central component of my research program is the use of biomarkers and biological signatures to improve diagnosis, prognostication, and patient stratification in critical illness. I develop and apply biomarker-driven approaches to identify subphenotypes, characterize heterogeneity of treatment effect, and enrich clinical trials by targeting therapies to the patients most likely to benefit.  I lead and collaborate on large multicenter randomized trials and pragmatic studies using innovative designs, including cluster-randomized and Bayesian frameworks, and I integrate advanced causal inference and machine-learning methods to enhance trial efficiency and translation into practice. In parallel, I am deeply committed to building sustainable clinical research infrastructure, mentoring trainees and junior faculty, and advancing patient-centered, implementation-ready research through national and international collaborations.

headline: Sunny Bhatia, MD, is President and Chief Medical Officer of Prime Healthcare, an award-winning national hospital system with 51 tax paying and not for profit hospitals and more than 360 outpatient locations in 14 states. Prime Healthcare and Prime Healthcare Foundation, with over 2.5 million patient visits annually, have provided over $14 billion in charity and uncompensated care since 2010 and nearly $3 billion to modernize hospitals across the country.  Dr. Bhatia is an interventional cardiologist quadruple board-certified in Internal Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Nuclear Cardiology, and Interventional Cardiology. Dr. Bhatia is a Fellow of the American College of Cardiology and the Society for Cardiac Angiography and Interventions. Dr. Bhatia is also a Fellow of the American College of Healthcare Executives. He is also involved in charitable causes including the World Children’s Initiative and the Uganda Heart Project. Additionally, Dr. Bhatia established the Bhatia Family Scholarship for Future Community-Based Physicians at his alma mater, the University of Minnesota Medical School.  Dr. Bhatia also serves as CEO of Prime Healthcare Region I and Region VII which includes Prime’s 24 hospitals and affiliated entities located in California, Nevada and Illinois. In addition, he serves as the Chief Medical Officer at Sherman Oaks Hospital and Encino Hospital Medical Center, two of Prime Healthcare’s hospitals located in Los Angeles County.   Dr. Bhatia received his bachelor’s degree from the University of Pennsylvania. He obtained his medical degree from the University of Minnesota Medical School and completed an Internal Medicine Residency at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota where he received the Internal Medicine Outstanding Achievement Award. After completing a Cardiology fellowship at the University of Southern California, Dr. Bhatia pursued further specialty training in Interventional Cardiology. Dr. Bhatia also earned a Master of Medical Management from the USC Marshall School of Business, holds a Certificate in Healthcare Strategy from Harvard Business School, and serves as Associate Professor of Medical Education at the California University of Science and Medicine.  Dr. Bhatia received recognition as a 2023 CEO Visionary by LA Times and has been recognized by Becker’s Hospital Review as among the “100 CMOs to Know” for several years. In addition, he has received recognition as the Healthcare Innovator of the Year by The Millennium Alliance and as a “Top Doctor” and “Executive of the Year” in the LA Business Journal for multiple years.

Dr. Joseph Sakran is a trailblazer and nationally respected voice in the firearm injury prevention movement. He is currently the Executive Vice Chair of Surgery, Director of Clinical Operations, and Associate Professor of Surgery and Nursing at Johns Hopkins Medicine in Baltimore, Maryland.   As a survivor of firearm-related violence, he was motivated to become a surgeon, researcher, and advocate in firearm injury prevention. At every turn of his career, he has used his personal experience and substantial skills to push a new frontier primarily in service of marginalized communities in the United States. The Academy Health recognized his research on firearm-related injury with the Outstanding Article of the Year Award.   Dr. Sakran served as a National Academy of Medicine Robert Wood Johnson Health Policy Fellow in the U.S. Senate during the COVID-19 pandemic guiding historic legislation. As a Senior Fellow at the Satcher Health Leadership Institute, Dr. Sakran was instrumental in creation of the Health Equity Tracker. In 2019, Dr. Sakran was named a Presidential Leadership Scholar in which he furthered his research on safe gun storage. He was also a 2024  recipient of Johns Hopkins' President Frontier Award for his pioneering work on gun violence prevention.   He serves as the Chair and Chief Medical Officer of the board of Brady United. Joe was instrumental in helping shepherd the legislation that led to the passage of the first federal firearm injury prevention legislation in nearly 30 years, the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act. Dr. Sakran was influential in laying the foundation for the creation of the White House Office of Gun Violence Prevention that was launched by President Biden in September of 2023.   He has demonstrated & trained healthcare professionals on how to effectively communicate the data & science to drive social change. He has testified before U.S. Congress, and other Federal and State agencies on Firearm injury prevention. Most recently, he was elected to the National Academy of Medicine for his is innovative work and exceptional leadership in firearm injury prevention, which has been most instrumental in establishing the urgency and intellectual foundation to drive research and evidence-based policy change at the local, state, and federal level.

One area that has grown significantly in importance is procurement and vendor relations. Clients are arriving with much more structured expectations for how they source and qualify partners, and I work directly with their counterparts to navigate that well. I am also drawn to finding better tools when they can make a real difference. Using AI agents to surface therapeutic-area expertise and history from our consulting network has been one good example. That kind of work, finding where a small change removes meaningful friction, is something I genuinely enjoy.  When I am not working, I enjoy the quieter side of life with my husband, spending time with our two sons, and dog, Bree, with whom I admittedly spend an enormous amount of my free time.
